 SCCH.13 3 MVC.3572 & 3573/2022  COMMON JUDGMENT
These two claim petitions are filed  under Sec.166 Motor Vehicles Act 1989  seeking compensation for the death of  Dhanush H.S. and for the injuries sustained  by Asha in a road traffic accident.

2. The Petitioners in both the  petitions have stated that on 12022022  about 7.00 p.m., Dhanush H.S. was riding the  TVS XL Super Heavy Duty Bike bearing  Reg.No.KA45EC0862 along with his mother  Asha near Basaveshwara Temple, Naganahalli  Village, Periyapatna Taluk, Mysuru District,
 at that time, the rider of Honda CB bearing  No.KA09HZ2859 (hereinafter called as  offending vehicle) rode the same with high  speed, in a rash and negligent manner and  dashed to the TVS XL bike.
As a result, both  Dhanush H. S. and Asha were fell down and  sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately  after the accident, both were shifted to the  SCCH.13 4 MVC.3572 & 3573/2022  Periyapatna Govt. hospital, wherein after  first aid treatment referred Apollo BGS Srinivasa Gowda H.C vs Paramesha.B.K on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45431764/
2  Hospital, Mysore wherein injured Asha took  conservative treatment and Dhanush H.S.
 declared as dead by doctor and then in  Periyapatna Govt. hospital postmortem  examination done and then dead body was  handed over to the Petitioners. Further the  injured Asha referred to Kamakshi hospital,
 Kuvempunagar, Mysore, wherein she took  treatment as inpatient and underwent  surgery.

sentences.text: 3. Petitioners in MVC.3572/2022 have  stated that they have performed last rites  ceremony and obsequies by spending a sum  more than 1,00,000/.

Further they have  stated that the deceased was aged 18 years  at the time of accident and he was studying  Diploma course and was hale and healthy and  was a brilliant student use to participate  Cocurricular activities.

Petitioner No.1 &
 SCCH.13 5 MVC.3572 & 3573/2022  2 are the parents and Petitioner No.3 is  younger brother of deceased and they have  sought for compensation of 50,00,000/ for  the death of Dhanush H. S. from the  Respondents.
 4.

In MVC No.3573/2022 Petitioner has  stated that prior to the accident she was  hale and healthy aged about 35 years and was  a Vegetable vendor and earning 20,000/ per  month and due to the accidental injuries she
has suffered permanent disability and  suffered loss of income and earning  capacity.
She has sought for compensation of  12,00,000/ for injuries sustained by her  by the Respondents.
5. In response to the petition  notices, the Respondent No.2 has appeared  before the court through its counsel and  filed its written statement in both the  petitions.

The Respondent No.1 has failed to  SCCH.13 6 MVC.3572 & 3573/2022  appear before the Court, hence he has been Srinivasa Gowda H.C vs Paramesha.B.K on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45431764/
3  placed exparte.

6. The Respondent No.2 - insurer of  offending vehicle has stated in the written  statement that it has issued the policy to  the offending vehicle in favour of 1st  Respondent and its liability is subject to  terms and conditions of the policy.
It has  contended that the owner of the offending  car and the concerned police have not  complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
It has  denied the occurrence, mode of the accident  and also involvement of offending two  wheeler as alleged in the Petition.

It is  contended that the owner has entrusted the  vehicle to the person who had no valid and  effective driving licence and thereby the  first Respondent has breached the terms and  conditions of the policy.

It has denied the  age of deceased Dhanush H.S. and the  SCCH.13 7 MVC.3572 & 3573/2022  dependency of Petitioners and also denied  the age, occupation, income, and injuries  sustained by the Petitioner in  MVC.3573/2022, expenses incurred by her and  disability suffered by her. The compensation  claimed by Petitioners is highly exorbitant  and fanciful and prayed for dismissal of the  Petitions.
 7. On the basis of above pleadings,
 the following issues have been framed :-
 IN MVC.3572/2022  1. Whether the Petitioners prove

that the death of Dhanush H.S.
 S/o H.C. Srinivas Gowda was only  due to rash and negligent riding  by the rider of Honda CB bearing  No.KA09HZ2859 on 12022022  about 7.00 p.m., near  Basaveshwara Temple, on  Bettadapura Kitturu Road,
 Naganahalli village, Periyapatna  Taluk, Mysuru District?
 2.What compensation Petitioners  are entitled?

Whether the Petitioner proves  that she sustained injuries when  she was a pillion rider in TVS  XL Super Heavy Duty Bike bearing  No.KA45EC0862 on on 1202  2022 about 7.00 p.m., near  Basaveshwara Temple, on  Bettadapura Kitturu Road,
 Naganahalli village, Periyapatna  Taluk, Mysuru District only due  to rash and negligent riding by  the rider of Honda CB bearing  No.KA09HZ2859?
 2. What compensation Petitioner is  entitled?
3. What order?
8. As both the petitions arise out of  the same accident
, on the application made  by the parties, both the petitions were  clubbed and the common evidences were  recorded.

9. In order to substantiate the claim,
 the Petitioner No.2 in MVC.3572/2022 is  examined as PW.1, injured Petitioner in  MVC.3573/2022 is examined as PW.2.
Further  one witness is examined as PW3 and got  marked the documents as Ex.P1 to 22  respectively.
10. The Respondentinsurance company  has not lead rebuttal evidence.
11. I have heard the counsel on both  sides and have perused the material on  record.

 BOTH IN MVC.3572/2022 & MVC.3573/2022  Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.
Issue No.3:
Issue No.1 in both petitions:

Petitioners say that on 12022022 about  7.00 p.m., Dhanush H.S. was riding the TVS  XL Super Heavy Duty Bike bearing Reg.No.KA  45EC0862 along with his mother Asha near  Basaveshwara Temple, Naganahalli Village,
 Periyapatna Taluk, Mysuru District, at that  time, the rider of Honda CB bearing No.KA  09HZ2859 rode the same with high speed, in  a rash and negligent manner and dashed to  the TVS XL.

As a result, both Dhanush H.S.
 and Asha were fell down and sustained  grievous injuries.

Immediately after the  accident, both were shifted to the  Periyapatna Govt. hospital, wherein after  first aid treatment referred to Apollo BGS  Hospital, Mysore wherein injured Asha took  conservative treatment and Dhanush H.S.
 declared as dead by doctor.
Further the  injured Asha was referred to Kamakshi  hospital, Kuvempunagar, Mysore, wherein she  SCCH.13 11 MVC.3572 & 3573/2022  took treatment as inpatient and underwent  surgery.
14. The uncle of deceased gave first  information statement to the police as per  Ex.P2.
On the basis of the first information  statement, FIR was registered as Ex.P1, spot  mahazar was drawn and sketch was prepared as  per Ex.P3 and Ex.P4.
Inquest of the dead  body is done as per Ex.P.5.
Postmortem  report is produced at Ex.P6.

IMV report as  at ExP7 and charge sheet is produced at Srinivasa Gowda H.C vs Paramesha.B.K on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45431764/

 15.
The Respondent  insurance company  in its objections has contended that they  are not liable to pay any compensation as
the offending vehicle was not involved in  the accident and the driver of the offending  vehicle did not possess valid driving  licence at the time of accident.

They have  not taken any contention with regard to  negligence and other facts specifically it  SCCH.13 12 MVC.3572 & 3573/2022  is stated that they denied the occurrence  and mode of accident stated by
the  Petitioners
. During crossexamination of  PW1 and 2 it was suggested that the  deceased Dhanush had no DL.

He was not  wearing helmet, it was his negligence as he  was riding motorcycle without helmet and  without having DL due to which he sustained  severe head injury otherwise he would not  have died due to accidental injuries.

PW1  has denied the suggestions and contended  that he had also sustained injuries on the  chest and it was not his negligence.
 16.

On perusal of police records, it is  clear that the offending motorbike had hit  the motorcycle from the opposite side and  according to the sketch, it appears that it  was the negligence of rider of offending  motorbike alone as it has come on the  extreme right side and dashed the motorcycle  of the deceased.
Police have filed the  SCCH.13 13 MVC.3572 & 3573/2022  charge sheet against the rider of the  motorbike.
Moreover, the Respondent No.2 has  not lead any rebuttal evidence to disprove  the case of the Petitioners.
Petitioners  have proved that it was the negligence of  rider of the offending motorbike and the  evidence corroborate with the documents  produced by them.

Hence I hold that the  death of one Dhanush H.S. and injury to  Asha were only due to rash and negligent Srinivasa Gowda H.C vs Paramesha.B.K on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45431764/
7  riding by the rider of the alleged offending  motorbike and hence I have answered Issue  No.1 in both the petitions in the  Affirmative.
 17. Issue No.2 in MVC.3572/2022:
The  Petitioners states that they are the legal  heirs of the deceased Dhanush H.S..
The  Petitioner No.1 is the father, Petitioner  no.2 is the mother and Petitioner No.3 is  the younger brother of the deceased.
They  have produced their Aadhaar cards to show  SCCH.13 14 MVC.3572 & 3573/2022  the relationship.
On perusal of these  documents it appears that Petitioner No.1 is  the is the father, Petitioner no.2 is the  mother and Petitioner No.3 is the younger  brother of the deceased.
Therefore, the  Petitioners being parents and younger  brother of deceased are all considered as  Legal heirs.
18. In the petition they have stated  that deceased Dhanush H.S. was 18 years of  age and he was studying Diploma Course.
But  PW1 has not produced any documents in this  regard.
Considering that deceased was a  student, notional income of 15,500/ is  considered.
19. As per Ex.P.20 - Aadhaar Card of  deceased Dhanush H.S., his date of birth was  02092003, hence the age of the deceased is  19 years as on the date of accident.

Hence,
 the age of the deceased is considered as 19  SCCH.13 15 MVC.3572 & 3573/2022  years and appropriate multiplier applicable  is 18.
 20.

As the deceased was below 40 years  of age, future prospects of 40% is added on  the income of the deceased as per decision  of Hon'ble Supreme Court in National  Insurance Co. vs. Pranay Sethi (2017 ACJ  2700), it comes around .15,500/ + 6,200 =

 50% of his income shall be deducted towards  his personal and living expenses, as  observed in the decision of Hon'ble Supreme  Court in Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport  Corporation reported in 2009 ACJ 1298.

 .1,30,200/.

CONSORTIUM:

By following the  guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in  Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs Nanu  SCCH.13 16 MVC.3572 & 3573/2022  Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others1, this  Tribunal deems it proper to hold that the  Petitioners are entitled .40,000/ each  under the head of consortium and for loss of  love and affection as the Petitioner No.1  and 2 have lost their son and Petitioner  No.3 has lost his brother, who was support  for him. In total Petitioners are awarded  .1,20,000/ under loss of consortium and  loss of love and affection.
 22. Loss to estate:

is the loss of savings by the  deceased.
It appears that the Petitioner  No.1 and 2 have lost their son and  Petitioner No.3 has lost his brother.

Hence,
 .20,000/ towards loss to estate.
23. Transportation of dead body, funeral  and obsequies Expenses:

Petitioners have  stated in the petition that they have  incurred .2,00,000/ towards transportation  1  (2018) 18 SCC 130  SCCH.13 17 MVC.3572 & 3573/2022  of dead body, funeral & obsequies ceremony  expenses.
However, by considering the facts  and circumstances, it would be proper to  award .15,000/ for the transportation of  dead body, funeral & other incidental  expenses.

The  Petitioner states that she was aged about 35  years as on the date of accident.
Due to the  accident she has sustained grievous  SCCH.13 18 MVC.3572 & 3573/2022  injuries.
Immediately after the accident she  was taken to Periyapatna Government  hospital, further referred to Apollo BGS  Hospital wherein she took conservative  treatment.
Thereafter she was shifted to  Kamakshi Hospital, wherein she was treated  as an inpatient.
It is said that she  sustained head injury and fracture of the  lateral third of the left clavicle.
She has  stated that she was working as a Vegetable  vendor and earning .20,000/p.m. Due to the  accidental injuries she is unable to do the  said work.
She has lost her normal life as  earlier and suffering huge loss of income.

Dr. Nagaraj B.N., Orthopedic  surgeon at Sai Ortho & Dental Center,
 Bengaluru, has deposed that the Petitioner  has sustained injuries in a RTA and she was  treated at Kamakshi hospital, Mysore as an  inpatient twice.
Doctor has stated that she  has sustained head injury and fracture of  SCCH.13 19 MVC.3572 & 3573/2022  the lateral third of the left clavicle.

On  27092023 he examined the Petitioner for Srinivasa Gowda H.C vs Paramesha.B.K on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45431764/
10  disability assessment and found that now she  complains of unable to lift things in the  left hand, unable to do her routine work  comfortably and there is 10% of disability  to the left arm and disability of 10% to the  whole body.

Along with his evidence, doctor  has produced clinical notes and Xray at Ex  P21 and Ex.P.22.
 27.
In his crossexamination doctor has  stated that Petitioner had come only for  assessment of disability and he has not  given any treatment to the Petitioner.
Further stated that he had verified the  wound certificate and discharge summary and  the Petitioner was advised physiotherapy by  the treated doctor.

He has admitted that as  per recent Xray fracture is united;
 implants are in situ.
He denied that co  ordinate activities hindrance are due to  SCCH.13 20 MVC.3572 & 3573/2022  presence of implants.
Considering the injury  and age of the Petitioner and considering  the difficulties of the Petitioner,
functional disability of the Petitioner is  assessed at 10%.
28. The Petitioner has produced Aadhar  card Ex.P.11 to show her age.
According to  this document her year of birth is 1987 and  she was 35 years as on the date of accident.
By considering this document, her age is  considered as 35 years and multiplier  applicable is "16".
The Petitioner has  claimed that she was working as a Vegetable  vendor and earning .20,000/p.m.
But she  has not produced any documents to prove her  avocation and income.
Hence, considering  year of accident and age of the Petitioner  as on the date of accident, notional income  of .15,500/ is taken.

Therefore, Loss of  future earnings due to permanent disability  SCCH.13 21 MVC.3572 & 3573/2022  is calculated as .15,500 x 12 x 16 x 10% =
 2,97,600/.

11  29.
Pain and sufferings:

So far as the  compensation under nonpecuniary damages are  concerned, considering the fact that the  Petitioner has suffered head injury and  fracture of the lateral third of the left  clavicle, which caused her immeasurable  mental agony and pain, I am of the opinion  that an amount of 40,000/ would be just  and fair compensation under the head pain  and sufferings.
 30. Loss of amenities of life:
For loss  of amenities of life undoubtedly she has to  lead her life ahead and she is sure to  suffer on her day today activities and face  hardships.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded  .25,000/ under loss of amenities of life.
31. Medical expenses:

Under the  pecuniary damages, expenses relating to  SCCH.13 22 MVC.3572 & 3573/2022  treatment, hospitalization and medicines, in  support of this she has produced medical  bills at ExP19 amounting to .1,30,223/.
Insurance company has disputed the medical  bills.
On perusal of medical bills, it is  found that all advance receipts are included  along with the IP bills.
Hence, bills at  sl.no.7, 8, 21, 27 and 29 of Ex.P.19 total  amounting to 52,300/ are not considered as  they are included in the IP bill produced  at sl.no.2 and 3.

Hence, considering other  bills, Petitioner is awarded .77,923/
 under the head of medical expenses.
32. Future medical expenses:
PW3  doctor has stated that the Petitioner needs  one more surgery for removal of implants  which cost 60,000/.
But PW3 has not  produced any estimation in this regard.
In  the absence of clear estimation of the  future expenses, it would be proper to award  .15,000/ towards Future medical expenses.

Conveyance, food, nourishment and  attendant charges:

Ex. P.14 to 16Discharge  summaries show that the Petitioner has taken  treatment as an inpatient in Apollo BGS  hospital and Kamakshi Hospital, from  12.02.2022 to 20.02.2022 i.e., for a period  of 9 days.

Therefore, it is just and  reasonable to award compensation of  9,000/ under the head of conveyance,
 food, nourishment and attendant charges.
34. Loss of income during laid up  period:
With regard to loss of earnings  during treatment, considering the treatment  taken by the Petitioner it would be proper  to award 3 months income as loss of earnings  during treatment.
Hence, .46,500/ is  awarded towards Loss of earnings during laid  up period.

 36. Liability:
As it is already held in  issue No.1 that it was the negligence on the  part of the rider of the offending vehicle  in causing the accident, which was insured  with 2nd Respondent  insurance company.
Hence, the Respondents No.1 and 2 are  jointly and severally liable to pay the  compensation.

The policy was in existence as  on the date of accident and hence Respondent  No.2insurance company is liable to  SCCH.13 25 MVC.3572 & 3573/2022 Srinivasa Gowda H.C vs Paramesha.B.K on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45431764/
13  indemnify the claim of the injured  Petitioners with interest @ 6% p.a.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in both  the petitions partly in the affirmative.
37. Issue No.3 in both the cases
: In  view of the above discussion, reasons  stated and findings given to above Issues, I  proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R Both claim Petitions filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioners in MVC.3572/2022 are awarded compensation of 24,98,600/ together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the realisation.
Petitioner in MVC.3573/2022 is awarded compensation of 5,11,023/ together with interest @ 6% p.a. (future medical expenses does not carry interest) from the date of petition till the realisation.
Respondent No.2 insurer shall deposit the compensation amount within two months from the date of this Order.

After deposit of compensation amount in MVC.3572/2022, 3,00,000/ is apportioned to Petitioner No.3 and the same shall be kept in FD in his name in any nationalized or scheduled bank of 1st Petitioner's choice till he attains the age of majority.
Remaining award amount including entire interest shall be equally apportioned to Petitioner No.1 and 2.

Out of the said apportioned amount 25% each of the amount shall be kept in FD in the name of Petitioner No.1 and 2 for a period of 2 years and balance amount of 75% each shall be released in their favour through Epayment on proper identification.
Entire Compensation amount in MVC.3573/2022 shall be disbursed to the Petitioner through E payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/ each.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Immediately after the  accident, both were shifted to the  Periyapatna Govt. hospital, wherein after  first aid treatment referred to Apollo BGS  Hospital, Mysore wherein injured Asha took  conservative treatment and Dhanush H.S.
 declared as dead by doctor.
The Respondent  insurance company  in its objections has contended that they  are not liable to pay any compensation as
the offending vehicle was not involved in  the accident and the driver of the offending  vehicle did not possess valid driving  licence at the time of accident.
He was not  wearing helmet, it was his negligence as he  was riding motorcycle without helmet and  without having DL due to which he sustained  severe head injury otherwise he would not  have died due to accidental injuries.
On perusal of police records, it is  clear that the offending motorbike had hit  the motorcycle from the opposite side and  according to the sketch, it appears that it  was the negligence of rider of offending  motorbike alone as it has come on the  extreme right side and dashed the motorcycle  of the deceased.
Police have filed the  SCCH.13 13 MVC.3572 & 3573/2022  charge sheet against the rider of the  motorbike.
Moreover, the Respondent No.2 has  not lead any rebuttal evidence to disprove  the case of the Petitioners.
Petitioners  have proved that it was the negligence of  rider of the offending motorbike and the  evidence corroborate with the documents  produced by them.
By following the  guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in  Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs Nanu  SCCH.13 16 MVC.3572 & 3573/2022  Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others1, this  Tribunal deems it proper to hold that the  Petitioners are entitled .40,000/ each  under the head of consortium and for loss of  love and affection as the Petitioner No.1  and 2 have lost their son and Petitioner  No.3 has lost his brother, who was support  for him. In total Petitioners are awarded  .1,20,000/ under loss of consortium and  loss of love and affection.

Remaining award amount including entire interest shall be equally apportioned to Petitioner No.1 and 2.
Out of the said apportioned amount 25% each of the amount shall be kept in FD in the name of Petitioner No.1 and 2 for a period of 2 years and balance amount of 75% each shall be released in their favour through Epayment on proper identification.
Entire Compensation amount in MVC.3573/2022 shall be disbursed to the Petitioner through E payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/ each.
Draw award accordingly.
